speaker: Kimi K3
text: JPM's 18.6% five-year CAGR and 2.2% dividend yield make it a genuine compounder, but the 74% max drawdown means a single crisis can reset years of gains — exactly the risk a 10x quest can't afford. At 0.91 beta and only 1.8% excess return versus the S&P over the last year, it's essentially index exposure with bank-specific tail risk, not alpha. For your $100 sleeve, fractional shares remove the price barrier, yet the zero-commission round-trip still leaves you needing roughly 21% annualised just to hit the 10x in three years after ordinary-income tax on short-term gains. If you want financial-sector leverage with a cleaner balance sheet and higher ROE, a smaller position in a specialty insurer or payment processor would give more torque per dollar of risk.
